TUI-Journal

TUI-Journal is a terminal-based application that allows you to write and manage journal entries and notes from within the terminal. It supports storing entries in a local file (JSON) or a local database (SQLite) and provides a text-based user interface for creating, editing, searching, and organizing your entries.

Features
- Create, edit, and delete journal/notes entries from the terminal
- Store entries using a JSON file or a local SQLite database
- Search and filter entries, including fuzzy finding
- Built-in editor integration or use your preferred external editor
- Tagging, sorting, export/import of entries, and multi-select operations
- Cross-platform usage (Windows, macOS, Linux, BSD)

Usage
After installing the application (use platform packages or pre-built binaries for your system), run the command "tjournal" in your terminal.

Typical usage examples:
  $ tjournal
  $ tjournal --help

# TUI-Journal Custom Themes:

It's possible to override the styles used in the app or parts of them. Custom themes will be read from the file `theme.toml` in the configuration directory of `tui-journal`.

## Table of Contents

- [Getting Started](#getting-started)
- [Themes structures](#themes-structures)
  - [Themes Groups](#themes-groups)
  - [Themes Types](#themes-types)
    - [Color Type](#color-type)
    - [Style Type](#style-type)
- [Example](#example)

## Getting started:

To get started, users can use the provided CLI subcommands under `tjournal theme`. These include specifying the path for the themes file, printing the default themes to be used as a base, or writing the themes directly into the themes file.

```
Provides commands regarding changing themes and styles of the app

Usage: tjournal theme <COMMAND>

Commands:
  print-path      Prints the path to the user themes file [aliases: path]
  print-default   Dumps the styles with the default values to be used as a reference and base for user custom themes [aliases: default]
  write-defaults  Creates user custom themes file if doesn't exist then writes the default styles to it [aliases: write]
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## Themes structures:

### Themes Groups:

Themes are divided into the following groups:
- **general**: Styles for general controls in the app, including journal pop-ups, filter and sorting pop-ups, and more.
- **journals_list**: Styles for the main list of journals. These styles are differentiated from the general ones since they are more important and contain more information than general list items.
- **editor**: Styles for the built-in editor.
- **msgbox**: Colors for message-box prompts (Questions, Errors, Warnings, etc.).

### Themes Types:

The main types used to define themes are `Color` and `Style`.

#### Color Type

Represents the color value of an item or field. It can be defined as a terminal color, such as `Black` or `Reset`, or as an RGB value in hexadecimal format `#RRGGBB`.

#### Style Type

Represents a complete style definition with the following fields:
- **fg**: Foreground color.
- **bg**: Background color.
- **modifiers**: Modifiers change the way a piece of text is displayed. They are bitflags, so they can be easily combined.
  The available modifiers are: `BOLD | DIM | ITALIC | UNDERLINED | SLOW_BLINK | RAPID_BLINK | REVERSED | HIDDEN | CROSSED_OUT`.
- **underline_color**: The color of the underline parts if the `UNDERLINED` modifier is active.

Here is an example of a style with all elements defined:

```toml
# Example of a style with all possible elements
[example_style]
fg = "#0AFA96" # Foreground Color. Colors can be in hex-decimal format "#RRGGBB"
bg = "Black" # Background Color. Also it can be one of terminal colors.
# Modifiers with all available flags. Flags can be combined as in example.
modifiers = "BOLD | DIM | ITALIC | UNDERLINED | SLOW_BLINK | RAPID_BLINK | REVERSED | HIDDEN | CROSSED_OUT"
underline_color = "Magenta" # Color for underline element if activated  
```
It's worth mentioning that not all fields must be defined. Missing parts will be filled with their default values.

## Example:

Here is a small example of overriding some of the themes. For a full list of all available style fields, please use the CLI subcommands to print the default themes.

```toml
[general]
list_item_selected = { fg = "LightYellow", modifiers = "BOLD" }
input_block_active = { fg = "Blue" }

[general.input_block_invalid]
fg = "Red"
modifiers = "BOLD | SLOW_BLINK"

[general.input_corsur_active]
fg = "Black"
bg = "LightYellow"
modifiers = "RAPID_BLINK"

[general.list_highlight_active]
fg = "Black"
bg = "LightGreen"
modifiers = "UNDERLINED"
underline_color = "Magenta"

[journals_list.block_inactive]
fg = "Grey"
modifiers = ""

[journals_list.highlight_active]
fg = "Red"
bg = "LightGreen"
modifiers = "BOLD | ITALIC"

[journals_list.highlight_inactive]
fg = "Grey"
bg = "LightBlue"
modifiers = "BOLD"

[journals_list.title_active]
fg = "Reset"
modifiers = "BOLD | UNDERLINED"

[editor.block_insert]
fg = "LightGreen"
modifiers = "BOLD"

[editor.cursor_insert]
fg = "Green"
bg = "LightGreen"
modifiers = "RAPID_BLINK"

[msgbox]
error = "#105577"
question = "Magenta"
```

    tmp=tempfile.mkdtemp()

    for root,d,files in os.walk(tmp):
        print("  dir",root,d)

test(["-vvv","pc"])
test(["-vvvv","pc"])

test(["--version"])

import subprocess, time, os, tempfile
class TJ:
    def __init__(self, session="tj", args=None, config=None, json_content=None, sqlite=False, size=(120,40)):
        subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",session], capture_output=True)
        self.session=session
        self.tmp=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tjtest_")
        self.cfg=os.path.join(self.tmp,"cfg"); os.mkdir(self.cfg)
        if config is not None:
            open(os.path.join(self.cfg,"config.toml"),"w").write(config)
        self.home=os.path.join(self.tmp,"home"); os.mkdir(self.home)
        self.j=os.path.join(self.tmp,"entries.json")
        self.s=os.path.join(self.tmp,"entries.db")
        if json_content is not None:
            open(self.j,"w").write(json_content)
        backend_arg=f"-s {self.s}" if sqlite else f"-j {self.j}"
        if args is None: args=""
        cmd=f"HOME={self.home} TERM=xterm-256color /workspace/executable -c {self.cfg} {backend_arg} {args}"
        subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s",session,"-x",str(size[0]),"-y",str(size[1]),cmd])
        time.sleep(0.8)
    def pane(self):
        r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",self.session,"-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        return r.stdout
    def pane_e(self):
        r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",self.session,"-p","-e"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        return r.stdout
    def send(self, *keys, wait=0.4):
        for k in keys:
            # if length>1 and not special key name known, use -l literal?
            # tmux send-keys treats strings; we handle via caller splitting
            subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",self.session,k])
            time.sleep(0.05)
        time.sleep(wait)
    def send_text(self, text, wait=0.4):
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",self.session,"-l",text])
        time.sleep(wait)
    def kill(self):
        subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",self.session], capture_output=True)
    def show(self, label=""):
        print(f"\n=== {label} ===")
        print(self.pane())

use anyhow::Result;
use chrono::Local;
use log::{LevelFilter, Metadata, Record};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fs::{self, File, OpenOptions};
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::thread::{self, ThreadId};

use crate::settings::default_cache_log_path;

struct FileLogger {
    level: LevelFilter,
    file: Mutex<File>,
    thread_ids: Mutex<HashMap<ThreadId, usize>>,
}

impl FileLogger {
    fn thread_number(&self) -> usize {
        let id = thread::current().id();
        let mut map = self.thread_ids.lock().unwrap();
        let next = map.len() + 1;
        *map.entry(id).or_insert(next)
    }
}

impl log::Log for FileLogger {
    fn enabled(&self, metadata: &Metadata) -> bool {
        metadata.level() <= self.level
    }
    fn log(&self, record: &Record) {
        if !self.enabled(record.metadata()) {
            return;
        }
        let time = Local::now().format("%H:%M:%S");
        let tid = self.thread_number();
        let (rec_file, rec_line) = if record.target() == "tjournal::logging" {
            ("src/logging.rs", 38)
        } else {
            (record.file().unwrap_or(""), record.line().unwrap_or(0))
        };
        let level = format!("{:<5}", record.level().as_str());
        let level = level.trim_end_matches(|c| c == ' ' && record.level().as_str().len() == 5);
        // The reference logger (simplelog) pads short levels to 5 chars.
        let level_disp = format!("{:<5}", record.level().as_str());
        let _ = level;
        let line_text = format!(
            "{} [{}] ({}) {}: [{}:{}] {}\n",
            time,
            level_disp.trim_end(),
            tid,
            record.target(),
            rec_file,
            rec_line,
            record.args()
        );
        // simplelog actually keeps padding for INFO/WARN: [INFO ], [WARN ]
        let line_text = if record.level().as_str().len() < 5 {
            format!(
                "{} [{:<5}] ({}) {}: [{}:{}] {}\n",
                time,
                record.level().as_str(),
                tid,
                record.target(),
                rec_file,
                rec_line,
                record.args()
            )
        } else {
            line_text
        };
        if let Ok(mut f) = self.file.lock() {
            let _ = f.write_all(line_text.as_bytes());
            let _ = f.flush();
        }
    }
    fn flush(&self) {
        if let Ok(mut f) = self.file.lock() {
            let _ = f.flush();
        }
    }
}

pub fn level_for_verbosity(verbose: u8) -> LevelFilter {
    match verbose {
        0 => LevelFilter::Warn,
        1 => LevelFilter::Info,
        2 => LevelFilter::Debug,
        _ => LevelFilter::Trace,
    }
}

pub fn setup(log_path: Option<PathBuf>, verbose: u8) -> Result<()> {
    let path = log_path.unwrap_or_else(default_cache_log_path);
    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
        if !parent.as_os_str().is_empty() {
            fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
        }
    }
    let file = OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(&path)?;
    let level = level_for_verbosity(verbose);
    let logger = Box::new(FileLogger {
        level,
        file: Mutex::new(file),
        thread_ids: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
    });
    // If a logger was already installed (should not happen in this binary), ignore.
    if log::set_boxed_logger(logger).is_ok() {
        log::set_max_level(level);
    }
    if level == LevelFilter::Trace {
        log::trace!(target: "tjournal::logging", "Log initialized with level: TRACE");
    }
    Ok(())
}

import os, pty, subprocess, select, time, signal, tempfile, fcntl, termios, struct

time.sleep(0.5)

    if not r: break
    chunk=os.read(master,65536)
    if not chunk: break

os.write(master,b"q")
time.sleep(0.5)

while True:
    r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.2)
    if not r: break
    try: chunk=os.read(master,65536)
    except OSError: break
    if not chunk: break
    data2+=chunk
print("exit bytes", data2[-500:])
print("poll",p.poll())

use std::io;

use crate::event::{
    Event, KeyCode, KeyEvent, KeyEventKind, KeyEventState, KeyModifiers, KeyboardEnhancementFlags,
    MediaKeyCode, ModifierKeyCode, MouseButton, MouseEvent, MouseEventKind,
};

use super::super::super::InternalEvent;

// Event parsing
//
// This code (& previous one) are kind of ugly. We have to think about this,
// because it's really not maintainable, no tests, etc.
//
// Every fn returns Result<Option<InputEvent>>
//
// Ok(None) -> wait for more bytes
// Err(_) -> failed to parse event, clear the buffer
// Ok(Some(event)) -> we have event, clear the buffer
//

fn could_not_parse_event_error() -> io::Error {
    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Other, "Could not parse an event.")
}

pub(crate) fn parse_event(
    buffer: &[u8],
    input_available: bool,
) -> io::Result<Option<InternalEvent>> {
    if buffer.is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }

    match buffer[0] {
        b'\x1B' => {
            if buffer.len() == 1 {
                if input_available {
                    // Possible Esc sequence
                    Ok(None)
                } else {
                    Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(KeyCode::Esc.into()))))
                }
            } else {
                match buffer[1] {
                    b'O' => {
                        if buffer.len() == 2 {
                            Ok(None)
                        } else {
                            match buffer[2] {
                                b'D' => {
                                    Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(KeyCode::Left.into()))))
                                }
                                b'C' => Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(
                                    KeyCode::Right.into(),
                                )))),
                                b'A' => {
                                    Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(KeyCode::Up.into()))))
                                }
                                b'B' => {
                                    Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(KeyCode::Down.into()))))
                                }
                                b'H' => {
                                    Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(KeyCode::Home.into()))))
                                }
                                b'F' => {
                                    Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(KeyCode::End.into()))))
                                }
                                // F1-F4
                                val @ b'P'..=b'S' => Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(
                                    KeyCode::F(1 + val - b'P').into(),
                                )))),
                                _ => Err(could_not_parse_event_error()),
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    b'[' => parse_csi(buffer),
                    b'\x1B' => Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(KeyCode::Esc.into())))),
                    _ => parse_event(&buffer[1..], input_available).map(|event_option| {
                        event_option.map(|event| {
                            if let InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(key_event)) = event {
                                let mut alt_key_event = key_event;

                            }

                }
            }
        }
        b'\r' => Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(
            KeyCode::Enter.into(),
        )))),
        // Issue #371: \n = 0xA, which is also the keycode for Ctrl+J. The only reason we get
        // newlines as input is because the terminal converts \r into \n for us. When we
        // enter raw mode, we disable that, so \n no longer has any meaning - it's better to
        // use Ctrl+J. Waiting to handle it here means it gets picked up later
        b'\n' if !crate::terminal::sys::is_raw_mode_enabled() => Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(
            Event::Key(KeyCode::Enter.into()),
        ))),
        b'\t' => Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(KeyCode::Tab.into())))),
        b'\x7F' => Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(
            KeyCode::Backspace.into(),
        )))),
        c @ b'\x01'..=b'\x1A' => Ok(Some(InternalEvent::Event(Event::Key(KeyEvent::new(

fn char_code_to_event(code: KeyCode) -> KeyEvent {
    let modifiers = match code {
        KeyCode::Char(c) if c.is_uppercase() => KeyModifiers::SHIFT,
        _ => KeyModifiers::empty(),
    };
    KeyEvent::new(code, modifiers)
}

use crate::symbols::{block, line};

/// Scrollbar Set
/// ```text
/// <--▮------->
/// ^  ^   ^   ^
/// │  │   │   └ end
/// │  │   └──── track
/// │  └──────── thumb
/// └─────────── begin
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
pub struct Set<'a> {
    pub track: &'a str,
    pub thumb: &'a str,
    pub begin: &'a str,
    pub end: &'a str,
}

pub const DOUBLE_VERTICAL: Set = Set {
    track: line::DOUBLE_VERTICAL,
    thumb: block::FULL,
    begin: "▲",
    end: "▼",
};

pub const DOUBLE_HORIZONTAL: Set = Set {
    track: line::DOUBLE_HORIZONTAL,
    thumb: block::FULL,
    begin: "◄",
    end: "►",
};

pub const VERTICAL: Set = Set {
    track: line::VERTICAL,
    thumb: block::FULL,
    begin: "↑",
    end: "↓",
};

pub const HORIZONTAL: Set = Set {
    track: line::HORIZONTAL,
    thumb: block::FULL,
    begin: "←",
    end: "→",
};

import sys,os,re
sys.path.insert(0,"/tmp")
from harness2 import *
BINARY=os.environ.get("TJ_BINARY","/workspace/executable")
import json
# Extract cursor position from ANSI: find cell with bg 15 (normal cursor), 10? in editor area, and mode/title, text lines.
def probe(keys, setup_text="hello world foo\nsecond line here\nthird"):
    app=TJ(json_content=json.dumps([{"id":0,"date":"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z","title":"A","content":setup_text,"tags":[],"priority":None}]))
    app.send("Tab")
    # Put cursor at a known place: enter edit, Ctrl-a, Escape is line start of last line maybe. Instead use arrows: Up Up Home as initial in Normal
    app.send("Up"); app.send("Up"); app.send("Home")
    for k in keys:
        if k=="TEXT:>": app.send_text(">")
        else: app.send(k)
    pane=app.pane(); ansi=app.pane_e(); content_lines=[]
    for l in pane.splitlines()[1:5]:
        # content area between second border at x37 and last
        content_lines.append(l[38:119] if len(l)>38 else l)
    title=pane.splitlines()[0][38:60] if pane else ""
    cur=None
    for y,l in enumerate(ansi.splitlines()):
        # Find cursor cell bg sequences 48;5;15 or 48;5;10(green edit) or 48;5;4 visual, extract preceding visible chars complexity. Print line repr segments
        if "48;5;15" in l or "48;5;10" in l or "48;5;4" in l:
            cur=(y,l)
    print(f"{keys} title={title.strip()} lines={content_lines} cursorline={cur}")
    app.kill()

    fn scrollbar_area(&self, area: Rect) -> Option<Rect> {
        match self.orientation {
            ScrollbarOrientation::VerticalLeft => area.columns().next(),
            ScrollbarOrientation::VerticalRight => area.columns().next_back(),
            ScrollbarOrientation::HorizontalTop => area.rows().next(),
            ScrollbarOrientation::HorizontalBottom => area.rows().next_back(),
        }
    }

    /// Calculates length of the track excluding the arrow heads
    ///
    /// ```plain
    ///        ┌────────── track_length
    ///  vvvvvvvvvvvvvvv
    /// <═══█████═══════>
    /// ```
    fn track_length_excluding_arrow_heads(&self, area: Rect) -> u16 {
        let start_len = self.begin_symbol.map_or(0, CellWidth::cell_width);
        let end_len = self.end_symbol.map_or(0, CellWidth::cell_width);
        let arrows_len = start_len.saturating_add(end_len);
        if self.orientation.is_vertical() {
            area.height.saturating_sub(arrows_len)
        } else {
            area.width.saturating_sub(arrows_len)
        }
    }

            state.viewport_content_length
        } else if self.orientation.is_vertical() {
            area.height as usize
        } else {
            area.width as usize
        }
    }

pub fn vertical_scrollbar() -> Scrollbar<'static> {
    Scrollbar::new(ScrollbarOrientation::VerticalRight).symbols(ratatui::symbols::scrollbar::Set {
        track: "│",
        thumb: "█",
        begin: "▲",
        end: "▼",
    })
}
pub fn horizontal_scrollbar() -> Scrollbar<'static> {
    Scrollbar::new(ScrollbarOrientation::HorizontalBottom).symbols(ratatui::symbols::scrollbar::Set {
        track: "─",
        thumb: "🬋",
        begin: "◄",
        end: "►",
    })
}

pub fn paragraph_wrapped_lines(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    if width == 0 {
        return vec![text.to_owned()];
    }
    let height = ((text.len() / width) + 5).min(200) as u16;
    let area = Rect::new(0, 0, width as u16, height);
    let mut buf = Buffer::empty(area);
    Paragraph::new(text)
        .wrap(Wrap { trim: true })
        .render(area, &mut buf);
    let mut out: Vec<String> = (0..height)
        .map(|y| {
            (0..width as u16)
                .map(|x| buf[(x, y)].symbol())
                .collect::<String>()
                .trim_end()
                .to_owned()
        })
        .collect();
    while out.last().map(|s| s.is_empty()).unwrap_or(false) {
        out.pop();
    }
    if out.is_empty() {
        out.push(String::new());
    }
    out
}

pub fn render_centered_text(frame: &mut Frame, area: Rect, text: &str, style: Style) {
    if area.width == 0 || area.height == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let lines = paragraph_wrapped_lines(text, area.width as usize);
    for (i, line) in lines.into_iter().take(area.height as usize).enumerate() {
        let w = str_width(&line).min(area.width as usize);
        let offset = ((area.width as usize).saturating_sub(w)).div_ceil(2);
        let rect = Rect {
            x: area.x + offset as u16,
            y: area.y + i as u16,
            width: w as u16,
            height: 1,
        };
        frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new(line).style(style), rect);
    }
}

def run(actions,label,entries=None):
  if entries is None: entries='[{"id":0,"date":"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z","title":"A","content":"hello","tags":[],"priority":1},{"id":1,"date":"2024-01-02T00:00:00Z","title":"B","content":"second","tags":[],"priority":null}]'
  app=TJ(args="-vvv",json_content=entries)
  logpath=os.path.join(app.home,".cache/tui-journal/tui-journal.log")
  def read(): return open(logpath).read() if os.path.exists(logpath) else ""
  before=read()
  for a in actions:
    if isinstance(a,tuple) and a[0]=="text": app.send_text(a[1])
    else: app.send(a)
  after=read(); new=after[len(before):]
  print("\n===",label,"===")
  for l in new.splitlines():
    if "tjournal::" in l or "backend::" in l: print(l)
  app.kill()

    fn push_history_before_change(&mut self) {
        let limit = self.settings.history_limit;
        if limit == 0 {
            self.undo_stack.clear();
            self.redo_stack.clear();
            return;
        }
        let snap = self.snapshot_now();
        self.undo_stack.push(snap);

    fn apply_snapshot(&mut self, target: Snapshot) -> Result<()> {
        // Apply a target snapshot by diffing it against the current state,
        // using the provider's add/remove/update operations.  Re-created
        // entries receive fresh ids from the provider.
        let current = self.entries.clone();
        let current_ids: HashSet<u32> = current.iter().map(|e| e.id).collect();
        let target_ids: HashSet<u32> = target.entries.iter().map(|e| e.id).collect();
        let mut id_map: std::collections::HashMap<u32, u32> = std::collections::HashMap::new();

        // Remove entries that are not in the target.
        for entry in &current {
            if !target_ids.contains(&entry.id) {
                self.provider.remove_entry(entry.id)?;
            }
        }
        // Update entries present in both whose data differs.
        for t in &target.entries {
            if let Some(cur) = current.iter().find(|e| e.id == t.id) {
                if cur != t {
                    self.provider.update_entry(t)?;
                }
                id_map.insert(t.id, t.id);
            }
        }
        // Retained entries keep their current in-memory order; restored
        // entries are appended.
        let mut new_entries: Vec<Entry> = Vec::new();
        for entry in &current {
            if target_ids.contains(&entry.id) {
                if let Some(t) = target.entries.iter().find(|e| e.id == entry.id) {
                    new_entries.push(t.clone());
                }
            }
        }
        for t in &target.entries {
            if !current_ids.contains(&t.id) {
                let created = self.provider.add_entry(EntryDraft::from(t))?;
                id_map.insert(t.id, created.id);
                new_entries.push(created);
            }
        }
        self.entries = new_entries;
        let selected = target
            .selected_id
            .and_then(|id| id_map.get(&id).copied());
        // Keep filters etc., reselect by mapped id.
        let keep = selected;
        self.list_state.select(Some(0));
        self.refresh_displayed(keep);
        if let Some(id) = keep {
            self.select_entry_by_id(id);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

        if let Some(target) = self.undo_stack.pop() {
            let current = self.snapshot_now();
            match self.apply_snapshot(target) {
                Ok(()) => {
                    self.redo_stack.push(current);
                }
                Err(err) => self.show_error(format!("{}", err)),
            }
        }

    fn redo(&mut self) {
        if let Some(target) = self.redo_stack.pop() {
            let current = self.snapshot_now();
            match self.apply_snapshot(target) {
                Ok(()) => {
                    self.undo_stack.push(current);
                    let limit = self.settings.history_limit;
                    if limit > 0 {
                        while self.undo_stack.len() > limit { self.undo_stack.remove(0); }
                    }
                }
                Err(err) => self.show_error(format!("{}", err)),
            }

pub fn run(settings: Settings, styles: AppStyles, pending: PendingCommand) -> Result<()> {
    // Install a panic hook that restores the terminal before printing.
    let original_hook = std::panic::take_hook();
    std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(move |info| {
        let _ = disable_raw_mode();
        let _ = execute!(io::stdout(), LeaveAlternateScreen);
        original_hook(info);
    }));

    let result = run_inner(settings, styles, pending);
    // Restore terminal state (idempotent for the early-error paths).
    let _ = disable_raw_mode();
    let _ = execute!(io::stdout(), LeaveAlternateScreen);

fn run_inner(settings: Settings, styles: AppStyles, pending: PendingCommand) -> Result<()> {
    enable_raw_mode()?;
    let mut stdout: Stdout = io::stdout();
    execute!(stdout, EnterAlternateScreen)?;
    let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stdout);
    let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;

    // Creating the SQLite provider can fail (bad file etc.); on error the
    // caller restores the terminal before the error reaches main.
    let provider: Box<dyn DataProvider> = match settings.backend_type {
        BackendType::Json => Box::new(JsonDataProvider::new(settings.json_backend.file_path.clone())),
        BackendType::Sqlite => Box::new(SqliteDataProvider::new(settings.sqlite_backend.file_path.clone())?),
    };

    let (persisted, state_error) = load_persisted_state(&settings.app_state_dir);
    let persisted_sort = SortOptions {
        order: persisted.sorter.order,
        criteria: persisted.sorter.criteria.clone(),
    };
    let persisted_full_screen = persisted.full_screen;

    let mut app = App {
        settings,
        styles,
        provider,
        entries: Vec::new(),
        displayed: Vec::new(),
        list_state: ListState::default(),
        current_id: None,
        focus: Focus::EntriesList,
        editor: Editor::default(),
        full_screen: persisted_full_screen,
        multi_select: false,
        multi_selected: HashSet::new(),
        filter: None,
        sort: persisted_sort,
        popups: Vec::new(),
        should_quit: false,
        undo_stack: Vec::new(),
        redo_stack: Vec::new(),
    };

    app.initial_load(&mut terminal, pending, state_error)?;

    loop {
        terminal.draw(|frame| ui::draw(frame, &mut app))?;
        if app.should_quit {
            break;
        }
        let event = event::read()?;
        match event {
            Event::Key(key) => {
                if key.kind == KeyEventKind::Release {
                    continue;
                }
                app.handle_key(key, &mut terminal)?;
            }
            Event::Mouse(_) => {}
            Event::Resize(_, _) => {}
            Event::Paste(text) => {
                app.handle_paste(text);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    save_persisted_state(&app.settings.app_state_dir, &app.sort, app.full_screen);
    Ok(())
}

fn build_tag_lines(app: &App, entry: &Entry, width: usize, is_selected: bool) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
    let default_style = app.styles.journals_list.tags_default.to_rat();
    // Build a single styled line of all tags joined by separators.
    let mut spans: Vec<Span<'static>> = Vec::new();
    if is_selected {
        spans.push(Span::raw(entry.tags.join(" | ")));
    } else if !app.settings.colored_tags {
        spans.push(Span::styled(entry.tags.join(" | "), default_style));
    } else {
        let all_tags = app.all_tags();
        for (i, tag) in entry.tags.iter().enumerate() {
            if i > 0 {
                spans.push(Span::styled(" | ".to_owned(), default_style));
            }
            let palette_idx = all_tags.iter().position(|t| t == tag).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
            let tag_style = if palette_idx < TAG_PALETTE.len() {
                Style::default().fg(Color::Black).bg(TAG_PALETTE[palette_idx])
            } else {
                Style::default()
            };
            spans.push(Span::styled(tag.clone(), tag_style));
        }
    }
    // A word longer than the available width is placed on its own line
    // (following a blank line) and truncated by the list rendering, as in
    // the reference; span-at-a-time wrapping reproduces that.
    let has_long_word = entry
        .tags
        .iter()
        .any(|tag| tag.split(' ').any(|w| str_width(w) > width));
    if has_long_word && width > 0 {
        let mut lines: Vec<Line<'static>> = Vec::new();
        let mut current: Vec<Span<'static>> = Vec::new();
        let mut current_w = 0usize;
        for span in spans {
            let w = str_width(&span.content);
            if current_w + w > width {
                lines.push(Line::from(std::mem::take(&mut current)));
                current_w = 0;
            }
            let mut span = span;
            if w > width + 1 {
                let mut truncated = String::new();
                let mut tw = 0usize;
                for ch in span.content.chars() {
                    let cw = unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
                    if tw + cw > width + 1 { break; }
                    truncated.push(ch);
                    tw += cw;
                }
                span.content = truncated.into();
            }
            current.push(span);
            current_w += w;
        }
        if !current.is_empty() {
            lines.push(Line::from(current));
        }
        while lines.len() > 1 {
            let last_empty = lines
                .last()
                .map(|l: &Line| l.spans.iter().all(|s| s.content.is_empty()))
                .unwrap_or(false);
            if last_empty {
                lines.pop();
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        return lines;
    }
    wrap_styled_line(Line::from(spans), width)
}

fn wrap_styled_line(line: Line<'static>, width: usize) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
    if width == 0 {
        return vec![line];
    }
    let total_width: usize = line.spans.iter().map(|s| str_width(&s.content)).sum();
    let height = ((total_width / width) + 3).min(200) as u16;
    let area = Rect::new(0, 0, width as u16, height);
    let mut buf = Buffer::empty(area);
    Paragraph::new(Text::from(line))
        .wrap(Wrap { trim: false })
        .render(area, &mut buf);
    let mut lines: Vec<Line> = Vec::new();
    for y in 0..height {
        let mut spans: Vec<Span<'static>> = Vec::new();
        for x in 0..width as u16 {
            let cell = &buf[(x, y)];
            let symbol = cell.symbol();
            if symbol.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let style = cell.style();
            if let Some(last) = spans.last_mut() {
                let last_span: &mut Span<'static> = last;
                if last_span.style == style {
                    last_span.content.to_mut().push_str(symbol);
                    continue;
                }
            }
            spans.push(Span::styled(symbol.to_owned(), style));
        }
        // Drop trailing default-styled spaces.
        while let Some(last) = spans.last() {
            if last.style == Style::default() && last.content.trim().is_empty() {
                spans.pop();
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        if let Some(last) = spans.last_mut() {
            if last.style == Style::default() {
                let trimmed = last.content.trim_end().to_owned();
                last.content = trimmed.into();
            }
        }
        if spans.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        lines.push(Line::from(spans));
    }
    if lines.is_empty() {
        lines.push(Line::from(""));
    }
    lines
}

use crossterm::event::{KeyCode, KeyEvent, KeyModifiers};
use ratatui::{
    buffer::Buffer,
    layout::Rect,
    style::Style,
    widgets::{Block, Borders, Paragraph, Widget},
};
use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;

use crate::themes::AppStyles;

/// A single-line text input modelled on the behaviour used in the dialogs:
/// grapheme-naive (char based), with a visible cursor cell when active and
/// horizontal scrolling so the cursor stays in view.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct TextInput {
    text: String,
    /// Cursor position as a char index (0..=len).
    cursor: usize,
    scroll: usize, // first visible char index
    undo_stack: Vec<(String, usize)>,
    redo_stack: Vec<(String, usize)>,
}

impl TextInput {
    pub fn new(text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let text = text.into();
        let cursor = text.chars().count();
        Self { text, cursor, scroll: 0, undo_stack: Vec::new(), redo_stack: Vec::new() }
    }
    pub fn with_cursor_at_start(text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let mut s = Self::new(text);
        s.cursor = 0;
        s
    }
    pub fn text(&self) -> &str { &self.text }
    pub fn set_text(&mut self, text: impl Into<String>) {
        self.text = text.into();
        self.cursor = self.text.chars().count();
        self.scroll = 0;
        self.undo_stack.clear();
        self.redo_stack.clear();
    }
    pub fn cursor(&self) -> usize { self.cursor }

    fn chars(&self) -> Vec<char> { self.text.chars().collect() }
    fn byte_of(&self, char_idx: usize) -> usize {
        if char_idx == 0 { return 0; }
        self.text.char_indices().nth(char_idx).map(|(b, _)| b).unwrap_or(self.text.len())
    }
    pub fn insert_char(&mut self, ch: char) {
        let b = self.byte_of(self.cursor);
        self.text.insert(b, ch);
        self.cursor += 1;
    }
    pub fn backspace(&mut self) {
        if self.cursor > 0 {
            self.cursor -= 1;
            let b = self.byte_of(self.cursor);
            self.text.remove(b);
        }
    }
    pub fn delete(&mut self) {
        if self.cursor < self.text.chars().count() {
            let b = self.byte_of(self.cursor);
            self.text.remove(b);
        }
    }
    pub fn move_left(&mut self) { self.cursor = self.cursor.saturating_sub(1); }
    pub fn move_right(&mut self) {
        if self.cursor < self.text.chars().count() { self.cursor += 1; }
    }
    fn is_word(ch: char) -> bool { ch.is_alphanumeric() || ch == '_' }
    pub fn move_word_left(&mut self) {
        let chars = self.chars();
        let mut i = self.cursor;
        while i > 0 && !Self::is_word(chars[i - 1]) { i -= 1; }
        while i > 0 && Self::is_word(chars[i - 1]) { i -= 1; }
        self.cursor = i;
    }
    pub fn move_word_right(&mut self) {
        let chars = self.chars();
        let mut i = self.cursor;
        while i < chars.len() && !Self::is_word(chars[i]) { i += 1; }
        while i < chars.len() && Self::is_word(chars[i]) { i += 1; }
        self.cursor = i;
    }
    pub fn delete_word_left(&mut self) {
        let start = self.cursor;
        self.move_word_left();
        let from = self.byte_of(self.cursor);
        let to = self.byte_of(start);
        self.text.drain(from..to);
    }
    pub fn delete_word_right(&mut self) {
        let start = self.cursor;
        let from = self.byte_of(start);
        self.move_word_right();
        let to = self.byte_of(self.cursor);
        self.cursor = start;
        if to > from { self.text.drain(from..to); }
    }

    /// Handle a key; returns true if consumed as editing/movement.
    pub fn handle_key(&mut self, key: KeyEvent) -> bool {
        let ctrl = key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL);
        if ctrl && key.code == KeyCode::Char('u') {
            if let Some((text, cursor)) = self.undo_stack.pop() {
                self.redo_stack.push((self.text.clone(), self.cursor));
                self.text = text;
                self.cursor = cursor;
            }
            return true;
        }
        if ctrl && key.code == KeyCode::Char('r') {
            if let Some((text, cursor)) = self.redo_stack.pop() {
                self.undo_stack.push((self.text.clone(), self.cursor));
                self.text = text;
                self.cursor = cursor;
            }
            return true;
        }
        let before_text = self.text.clone();
        let before_cursor = self.cursor;
        let handled = self.handle_key_inner(key);
        if handled && self.text != before_text {
            self.undo_stack.push((before_text, before_cursor));
            self.redo_stack.clear();
        }
        handled
    }

    fn handle_key_inner(&mut self, key: KeyEvent) -> bool {
        let ctrl = key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL);
        let alt = key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::ALT);
        match key.code {
            KeyCode::Char(ch) if ctrl => {
                match ch {
                    'a' => { self.cursor = 0; true }
                    'e' => { self.cursor = self.text.chars().count(); true }
                    'f' => { self.move_right(); true }
                    'b' => { self.move_left(); true }
                    'd' => { self.delete(); true }
                    'h' => { self.backspace(); true }
                    'k' => {
                        let b = self.byte_of(self.cursor);
                        self.text.truncate(b);
                        true
                    }
                    'u' => { self.text.clear(); self.cursor = 0; true }
                    'w' => { self.delete_word_left(); true }
                    ' ' => false,
                    't' => false,
                    _ => false,
                }
            }
            KeyCode::Char(ch) if alt => {
                match ch {
                    'f' => { self.move_word_right(); true }
                    'b' => { self.move_word_left(); true }
                    'd' => { self.delete_word_right(); true }
                    _ => false,
                }
            }
            KeyCode::Char(ch) => { self.insert_char(ch); true }
            KeyCode::Backspace => {
                if alt { self.delete_word_left(); } else { self.backspace(); }
                true
            }
            KeyCode::Delete => { self.delete(); true }
            KeyCode::Left => {
                if ctrl { self.move_word_left(); } else if alt { return true; } else { self.move_left(); }
                true
            }
            KeyCode::Right => {
                if ctrl { self.move_word_right(); } else if alt { return true; } else { self.move_right(); }
                true
            }
            KeyCode::Home => { self.cursor = 0; true }
            KeyCode::End => { self.cursor = self.text.chars().count(); true }
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    pub fn render(&mut self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, title: &str, active: bool, invalid: bool, styles: &AppStyles) {
        let block_style = if invalid {
            styles.general.input_block_invalid.to_rat()
        } else if active {
            styles.general.input_block_active.to_rat()
        } else {
            Style::default()
        };
        let block = Block::default().borders(Borders::ALL).title(title.to_owned()).style(block_style);
        let inner = block.inner(area);
        Widget::render(block, area, buf);
        if inner.width == 0 || inner.height == 0 { return; }
        // Horizontal scroll so that the cursor is visible.
        let width = inner.width as usize;
        if self.cursor < self.scroll { self.scroll = self.cursor; }
        // Compute display widths from scroll to cursor.
        let chars = self.chars();
        let disp_width = |from: usize, to: usize, chars: &[char]| -> usize {
            chars[from..to].iter().map(|c| UnicodeWidthChar::width(*c).unwrap_or(0)).sum()
        };
        while self.scroll < self.cursor && disp_width(self.scroll, self.cursor, &chars) >= width {
            self.scroll += 1;
        }
        // Build the visible string.
        let mut visible = String::new();
        let mut used = 0usize;
        let mut idx = self.scroll;
        while idx < chars.len() {
            let w = UnicodeWidthChar::width(chars[idx]).unwrap_or(0);
            if used + w > width { break; }
            visible.push(chars[idx]);
            used += w;
            idx += 1;
        }
        let style = Style::default();
        let para = Paragraph::new(visible).style(style);
        Widget::render(para, inner, buf);
        if active {
            // Cursor cell: the char under the cursor, or a trailing space.
            let cursor_disp = disp_width(self.scroll, self.cursor.min(chars.len()), &chars);
            if cursor_disp < width {
                let x = inner.x + cursor_disp as u16;
                let y = inner.y;
                let cstyle = if invalid { styles.general.input_corsur_invalid.to_rat() } else { styles.general.input_corsur_active.to_rat() };
                let cell = &mut buf[(x, y)];
                if self.cursor >= chars.len() {
                    cell.set_symbol(" ");
                }
                cell.set_style(cstyle);
            }
        }
    }
}
